newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian advance guard arrives in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italian advance guard arrives in Albania.

text.p: Italian soldiers arrived in Albania on Friday to spearhead a multinational force that aims to secure key harbours and Tirana's airport in the poor Balkan country racked by weeks of armed anarchy.

An advance party of 20 Italian troops marched proudly onto a pier in the western port of Durres just after dawn at the start of a mission marking the first time Italy has led a multinational force in post-war history.

"Our mission does not rule out risks, but we hope the Albanian people will understand that we are here to help them," said Colonel Enrico Nardi, commander of the Italian landing unit in Durres, 40 (25 miles) west of Tirana.
Four Lockheed C130 Hercules aircraft carrying more than 50 paratroopers arrived at Tirana's airport during the morning.

The Italian troops were preparing the ground for a 6,000-strong force from six nations that is due to start arriving in Albania on Monday. In addition to the Italians, soldiers from France, Spain, Romania, Turkey and Greece are coming to Albania to help safeguard deliveries of emergency food and medical supplies.
The armed lawlessness that has left more than 200 dead and 700 injured since several fraudulent pyramid investment schemes collapsed claimed more casualties on Friday.
A 16-year-old boy was killed in a village near the southern town of Vlore when a grenade he was playing with exploded. A 15-year-old boy was seriously injured in the blast.

Several others were hurt in a gun battle between police and a gang in Fier, 110 km south of Tirana. Two armed men stormed a town meeting and tried to take control. The two were backed by about 15 others shooting their rifles into the sky.
After a gun battle with police, the gang commandeered a police armoured personnel carrier (APC) and escaped.
In the northern town of Shkoder, hospital workers demonstrated on Friday against the violence after two doctors were shot and wounded in a daylight attack at the hospital.
More than 200 people have been killed since rebels took control of the south last month in an eruption of anger following the collapse of the savings schemes.
Army arsenals were looted after soldiers and police abandoned their posts while automatic rifles and weapons were seized by citizens who brandished them on streets.

The Italian troops arrived in Durres smiling. They talked with journalists for about an hour. Standing under clear blue skies on the pier next to the brilliant turquoise Adriatic, they also handed pieces of candy to local children.
"We plan to check the road between Durres and Tirana and perhaps the airport," he added.

Only a handful of Albanians, who have been waiting for more than one month in vain for international help, were on hand to witness the Italians' arrival. The mission has attracted little attention in the local media.

"All this for only 20 soldiers?" asked a 50-year-old port worker named Besim as he watched some 40 foreign journalists and camera crews scramble to interview the soldiers on the pier. "There are more journalists than soldiers."

The Italian naval vessel, the Pantellaria, that carried the advance unit was escorted by a small Italian minesweeper, the Rimini. They steamed into Durres shortly after 8 a.m. (0600 GMT) and the minesweeper returned to Italy.

Asked by one Italian reporter if he knew that Italy's fascist leader Benito Mussolini sent troops to occupy Albania through the Durres port 58 years ago this month, another officer, a captain named Giorgio, shrugged his shoulders.
"I don't know what happened then, but I am sure we are here to help people in need," he said.

The soldiers at Tirana airport included a team of special forces with orders to secure the perimeter and a group of specialists whose job is to ensure the airport can operate round the clock and not just during daylight hours as at present.
